what_happened: The operator edited athena.toml by hand and raised the verifier time limit (`[budget] verifier_timeout_s`) from 1200 s to 2400 s. Two spec jobs in a row (20261018-120736-90w3 and 20261018-133651-1ncn) lost their verdict because the verifier hit the 1200 s limit. The full test suite now takes about 11 minutes, and the verifier reruns it before judging, so little time was left for judging. No job was involved, and the event is logged as an intervention.
cause: The verifier's time budget is a fixed number that no one ties to how long the checks take. The verifier also reruns checks that were already run and recorded, so its time need grows with the test suite. When the suite grew, nothing warned that the limit had become too tight. Nothing separated a timeout from a real failure either. Two verdicts were lost before anyone noticed, and the only fix was a manual config edit.
prevention: Make the verifier reuse the check results already recorded for the same snapshot instead of rerunning the suite, so its time goes to judging criteria. Also make a verifier timeout its own outcome. It should keep partial judgments and retry or resume the job, not reject it with every criterion unmet. Add a pre-check that compares the recorded suite duration with verifier_timeout_s and warns when too little time is left for judging.
proposed_request: Change the verifier so it reuses the recorded check results (test suite, lint and similar) for the exact snapshot being judged and does not rerun them. It should rerun a check only when no recorded result exists for that snapshot. Make a verifier deadline overrun a distinct outcome ("verifier timed out") that keeps any criterion verdicts already reached and lets the job be retried or resumed, without being counted as a rejection. Add an admission or startup warning when the recorded full-suite duration is more than half of [budget] verifier_timeout_s. Acceptance: (1) a verifier run on a snapshot with recorded passing checks starts no test-suite process, shown by a test; (2) a simulated deadline overrun gives the timed-out outcome with partial verdicts saved and is not recorded as a rejection; (3) the warning appears for a config where the suite duration exceeds half the timeout. After it lands, the verifier_timeout_s value can go back to a smaller number in a separate change.
